《字林西报》，1934年12月18日，星期二

赤匪斩首
美国人

斯坦姆夫妇的悲惨命运

公开处决

婴儿因一位传教士的英勇行为而得救

芜湖，12月16日电。
今日披露，处决约翰·C·斯坦姆（John C. Stam）牧师及其妻子伊丽莎白·斯坦姆（Elizabeth Stam）夫人，是中国共产党人对所有外国人开展死亡战役的第一步行动。
抵达此地的中国内地会（China Inland Mission）收到了关于这两位殉难美国传教士被谋杀的详细情况，这些细节显示，赤匪于12月8日发布告示，宣布必须处死斯坦姆夫妇，以此作为对其他“洋鬼子”的警示。
该告示称：“外国人损害中国，并帮助政府修筑道路。”“外国人为中国与其他国家制造麻烦。”
告示中声明“不需要赎金”，这驳斥了传教士在皖南景德镇（Tsingteh）遭遇突然袭击被捕后随即流传的、称他们被扣押以索取2万美元赎金的报道。
若非一位中国布道员罗牧师（Rev. Mr. Lo）的英勇行为，这对被杀害夫妇三个月大的女儿海伦·斯坦姆（Helen Stam）婴儿，可能会与其父母遭受同样的可怕命运，她的父母是被公开斩首的。
斯坦姆夫妇以某种尚不清楚的方式，成功将婴儿藏在庙首（Miaoshao）的一间空屋里。斯坦姆夫人在她和丈夫踏上通往刑场的勇敢旅程之前，用自己的衣物将孩子紧紧包裹保暖，并在海伦的衣服里别了一张10元钞票，留给施救者。

传教士救出婴儿
中国内地会芜湖站的罗牧师自愿冒着生命危险去调查斯坦姆夫妇的命运，他刚一踏进庙首就被共产党人抓获，但在短暂拘留后被释放。
得知海伦婴儿还活着后，罗先生经过长时间搜寻，在那间空屋里找到了她；在独自度过近24小时后，孩子安然无恙，正发出欢快的咿呀声。
使所有女性息息相通的母爱纽带证明比赤匪的恐怖更强大，在罗先生发现婴儿后的两天里，几位庙首的中国母亲敢于频繁前往婴儿的藏身之处探望。
在这两天里，这些中国志愿母亲用自己的乳汁喂养这名失去母亲的美国婴儿，而此时共产党军队正在不到三英里外与政府军激战，抢劫的赤匪涌过村庄。
据罗先生获悉，斯坦姆夫妇的处决是公开进行的，共产党首领邀请庙首的农民“观看洋鬼子死去”。

一名中国基督徒为这对注定死亡的夫妇求情。他在行刑队指挥官面前跪下，恳求释放他们。结果遭到一脚踢开和一顿咒骂，他自己也成了囚犯。他的命运目前尚不清楚，但人们担心他也已被处决。
甚至一些非基督徒也大胆地为这位美国传教士及其妻子说话，但他们的请求换来的只有殴打和咒骂。
在大批人群面前——这些人被无情的“赤匪”强迫观看这一恐怖景象——斯坦姆夫妇以不可动摇的勇气走向死亡。目睹处决过程的庙首居民表示，这对夫妇面对刽子手的刀斧时表现出一种胜利般的信念，给村民留下了深刻印象。

发现遗体
在与政府军交战后，共产党人撤退，放弃了庙首，罗先生发现了殉难者的遗体。数十名男女，不分信仰，都帮助他准备棺材以便安葬。
大量人群参加了葬礼仪式，但其中只有三人是斯坦姆夫妇为之献身的信仰的信徒。当这位中国布道员向聚集的人群讲话时，他们低头祈祷。
他说：“他们来不是为了自己，而是为了向我们人民讲述上帝的爱。”“他们献出生命，是为了给你们带来基督里的救赎信息。不要忘记他们的信息。”
听众中有人哭泣。许多人痛骂赤匪。数十人围在布道员身边，表达对杀害一男一女的遗憾，这两人的善良和同情心赢得了众多中国朋友，而不问信仰差异。
罗先生和他的妻子尽可能快地穿越被赤匪蹂躏的地区，将海伦婴儿健康地带到芜湖，于周五抵达此地。在收到其外祖父母——济南长老会传教站（Presbyterian Mission at Tsinan）的C. E. 斯科特博士（Dr. C. E. Scott）及斯科特夫人关于孩子未来安排的指示之前，孩子正由当地的中国内地会站点照顾。
根据芜湖收到的最新报告，皖南局势依然危急。共产党大军现在威胁着景德镇（Tsingteh）、屯溪（Tunki）和其他中心，传教士们正尽可能迅速地撤离屯溪和兰溪（Lanki）。——合众社。

领事调查
南京，12月17日电。
第二名美国领事乔治·艾奇逊（George Atcheson）先生今日被派往芜湖，对斯坦姆夫妇被谋杀案进行彻底调查。他还将收集这对夫妇的遗物，并确保对其婴儿做出妥善安置。
小道格拉斯·詹金斯（Douglas Jenkins, Jr.）先生也是驻南京的美国领事，在接到斯坦姆一家落入赤匪手中的消息后，立即前往芜湖。由于持续缺乏来自皖南的确切消息，许多外国人无法返回该地区。——合众社。

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 18, 1934

RUTHLESS REDS

The story of the last moments of John and Elizabeth Stam is illumined by the calmness of the martyred couple and by the heroism of a Chinese pastor to whose devotion and courage their infant girl owes her life. Mrs. Stam, with the desperate ingenuity of a mother in her plight, managed to hide the baby in a deserted house. In spite of the certainty of her own fate, Mrs. Stam coolly made all preparations to protect the child against the rigours of the weather. Her foresight led her to attach a currency note to the child's clothing for the practical assistance of such rescuers as might by chance come across the deserted house in the little village of Miaoshao. A volunteer from the China Inland Mission at Wuhu, the Rev. Lo—his name is not described with any more precision—travelled to Miaoshao and was immediately captured by the Communists, but fortunately released. After a long search he found the baby girl who, although she had been for a whole day left to herself, was unharmed and happy. Mr. Lo was able to enlist the sympathy of Chinese women who braved the terrors of the Red invasion which to them was a no less fearsome ordeal, and for two days gave the motherless baby nourishment. The defeat of the Reds by the Government troops made the coast clear. Mr. Lo's wife—another Chinese heroine—had joined him and the baby was safely brought in to the Mission Station at Wuhu. Before he left Miaoshao, the brave Chinese pastor discovered the bodies of the martyred missionaries and buried them with due ceremony to which his eloquence contributed a most moving scene. It evoked the voluntary expression of deep regret for the deaths of two strangers whose good works among the people were sufficient passports to affection.

Thus ruthlessness in expression of the grim Communist creed was set off by simple friendliness and courage on the part of these humble Chinese villagers and by the undaunted heroism of the Chinese pastor and his wife. The story shows how altogether futile is the adoption of the cult which the Reds seek to fasten on the essentially good-natured people of this country. The diabolical cruelty of the slaughter of the two missionaries whose only fault was their race, was, perhaps, the measure of the desperation of these Communist outlaws, driven from the Province which they had helped to ravage for so long and hunted down by the Government troops. If the reports are accurate, it would seem that hostility to the Government has been lately based on the charge that the extensive road-making schemes instituted by General Chiang Kai-shek have foreign inspiration. The Govern-
ment has no reason to fear propaganda of this kind. The answer to it was surely given when, in defiance of the invaders, the men and women of Miaoshao helped the pastor to prepare coffins for the burial of the bodies of John and Elizabeth Stam. Nor is this surprising; the only hold which Communism has really been able to exert on the people has been that of practical attention to economic reconstruction. Their empty creed has not the means to make such efforts of stable value. Therefore, except by the grip of relentless terrorism, the Reds have found their position impossible to maintain. When once the Government has organized its resources—military and civil—with a reasonable degree of efficiency and resolution, the Communists are at a loss. That they are capable of much mischief, even in their scattered state, is clear from the deplorable reports from Anhwei and other places. That must be an urgent care of the Government.

This tragedy has occurred almost within hailing distance of Nanking. It acquires so much the more importance. Yet similar tragedies, involving not foreigners but Chinese citizens, are occurring wherever the trail of the Communists leads. It is not surprising therefore that General Chiang Kai-shek has consistently maintained that attention to the Communist menace is the prime duty of his Government. For, clearly, the breakdown of rural economy which forms the topic of discussion wherever China's general condition is examined, gives direct incitement to the Communists with their specious promises. By those promises they get a foothold among people who despair of official attention to the realities of the countryside's decay. Having gained the foothold and knowing their fundamental incapacity to rebuild, the Communists apply all the machinery of a bloodthirsty terrorism to maintain their dominance. Thus violence is their only creed and murder their only weapon. In their irresponsibility they endeavour to arouse old fanaticism by accusing the Government of an unholy alliance with foreigners. Fortunately, the events of the last few years have confirmed the people in a more accurate perception of the meaning of the presence of foreigners in the interior of China. The lives of men and women like the Stams are, for the Chinese whom they befriend, crushing answers to the folly of the Reds' crazy xenophobia. Nor is the Government in the least likely to belie its own intelligence by wavering before so shallow a charge. With this thought in mind, no doubt, the authorities at Nanking will promptly vindicate their own intention of giving the Provinces the peace which is so much desired by putting forth all their strength to round up these desperate Communist bands and deprive them of further means of afflicting the people. No better tribute to the heroic dead could be paid.

《字林西报》，1934年12月18日，星期二

残酷的赤匪

约翰和伊丽莎白·斯坦姆最后时刻的故事，因这对殉难夫妇的镇定以及一位中国牧师的英雄主义而显得光辉，这位牧师的奉献和勇气使他们的女婴得以保全性命。斯坦姆夫人凭借身处绝境的母亲所特有的拼命机智，设法将婴儿藏在一间空屋里。尽管确信自己命运已定，斯坦姆夫人仍冷静地做好了一切准备，以保护孩子免受严寒之苦。她的远见使她在孩子的衣服上附了一张纸币，以便为那些可能偶然在庙首小村发现这间空屋的施救者提供实际帮助。一位来自中国内地会芜湖站的志愿者——罗牧师（其名字未作更精确的描述）——前往庙首，随即被共产党人抓获，但幸获释放。经过长时间搜寻，他找到了这名女婴，虽然她被独自留下整整一天，却安然无恙且情绪愉快。罗先生得以唤起中国妇女的同情，她们冒着赤匪入侵的恐怖风险——这对她们来说同样是一场可怕的磨难——并在两天内为这名失去母亲的婴儿提供营养。政府军击败赤匪后，道路得以畅通。罗先生的妻子——另一位中国女英雄——加入了他，婴儿被安全带到芜湖的传教站。在离开庙首之前，这位勇敢的中国牧师发现了殉难传教士的遗体，并以适当的礼仪安葬了他们，他的雄辩为这一场景增添了极其感人的一幕。这引发了人们自发地对两位陌生人死亡的深切哀悼，他们在民众中的善行足以成为赢得爱戴的通行证。

因此，表达冷酷共产主义信条的残忍，与这些卑微中国村民的朴实友善和勇气，以及中国牧师及其妻子不屈不挠的英雄主义形成了鲜明对比。这个故事表明，赤匪试图强加给这个本质上性情温和的国家人民的崇拜体系是完全徒劳的。屠杀两名传教士的恶魔般残忍——他们唯一的过错是其种族——或许衡量了这些共产党亡命之徒的绝望程度，他们被赶出了长期协助蹂躏的省份，并遭到政府军的追捕。如果报道属实，似乎近期对政府的敌意是基于这样一种指控：蒋介石将军发起的大规模筑路计划受到外国势力的鼓动。政府没有理由害怕这种宣传。当庙首的男女不顾侵略者的威胁，帮助牧师准备棺材以安葬约翰和伊丽莎白·斯坦姆的遗体时，无疑已经给出了对此的回答。这并不令人惊讶；共产主义真正能够对人民施加的唯一影响，在于其对经济重建的实际关注。他们空洞的信条没有手段使这种努力具有稳定的价值。因此，除了依靠无情恐怖的掌控外，赤匪发现其地位无法维持。一旦政府以合理的效率和决心组织起其军事和民用资源，共产党人便束手无策。从安徽和其他地方传来的令人痛心的报告中可以清楚地看出，即使处于分散状态，他们仍能造成巨大危害。这必须是政府迫切关注的问题。

这场悲剧发生在几乎能听到南京呼声的距离之内。这使得它更加重要。然而，类似的悲剧，涉及的不是外国人而是中国公民，正随着赤匪的行踪在任何地方发生。因此，蒋介石将军一贯坚持认为，关注共产党威胁是其政府的首要职责，这并不奇怪。因为，显然，在审视中国总体状况时成为讨论话题的农村经济崩溃，直接煽动了带着虚伪承诺的共产党人。通过这些承诺，他们在那些对官方关注乡村衰败现实感到绝望的人中间获得了立足点。在获得立足点并深知其根本无力重建之后，共产党人运用血腥恐怖的所有机制来维持其统治。因此，暴力是他们唯一的信条，谋杀是他们唯一的武器。在他们不负责任的行为中，他们试图通过指责政府与外国人结成邪恶联盟来激起旧的狂热情绪。幸运的是，过去几年的事件证实了人民对 foreigners 在中国内地存在意义的更准确认知。像斯坦姆夫妇这样的人的生命，对于他们所结交的中国人来说，是对赤匪疯狂排外愚蠢行为的有力回击。政府也绝不可能因如此浅薄的指控而动摇，从而违背其自身的理智。毫无疑问，南京当局怀着这一想法，将迅速证明其给予各省渴望已久的和平的意图，即全力以赴围剿这些绝望的共产党帮派，剥夺他们进一步祸害人民的手段。这是对英勇逝者最好的致敬。

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, DECEMBER 17, 1934

HELEN STAM

Helen Stam's survival of the tragic
ordeal, which has cost her the lives
of her parents, is a wonderful event.
It awakens feelings of deep gratitude
for what must be a great mitigation
of the sorrow now afflicting the
bereaved families. The little girl has
been taken to Wuhu where it is
hoped she will be able quickly to
recover from the strain of her
terrible experiences. Young as she
is their effect must be physical
rather than mental. She happily must
be in blissful unconsciousness of the
tragedy in which she has been
moving. Those in whose care she
will in due course come will no
doubt do all they can to ensure for
her a happy and long life of use-
fulness. Spared as she has been
from sharing her parents' fate, it is
well understandable that they will
feel some special direction of Pro-
vidence in shaping her destiny.
That her life will be less eventful
than in this first year of its course
will be the hope generally expressed
in her behalf.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1934年12月17日，星期一

海伦·斯塔姆（Helen Stam）

海伦·斯塔姆在那场夺去其父母生命的悲惨磨难中幸存下来，实乃奇迹。这一事件唤起了人们深深的感激之情，因为这无疑极大缓解了那些失去亲人的家庭此刻所遭受的悲痛。这名小女孩已被送往芜湖，希望她能迅速从可怕经历带来的身心压力中恢复过来。尽管她年纪尚幼，这些经历的影响必然更多体现在身体而非精神层面。幸运的是，她对自己身处其中的悲剧想必仍处于 blissful unconsciousness（ blissful unconsciousness，此处指一种因无知而免受痛苦的幸福无意识状态）。日后负责照料她的人无疑将竭尽所能，确保她拥有一个幸福且有益于社会的漫长人生。既然她幸免于难，未与其父母同遭厄运，人们完全可以理解，他们会感到这是上天在塑造她的命运时给予了某种特别的指引。普遍寄予她的希望是，她此后的人生将不再像这生命之初的第一年那样充满变故。

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 16, 1934

TAKEN CAPTIVE
By KUNIKOS

Since the revolution there have been approximately 350 missionaries taken captive by bandits in various parts of China. Of these about 55 are known to have been killed, while the fate of several others is still uncertain, though hope that some of them have survived the terrible hardships they will have undergone is very slim. The number of hold-ups and robberies is very much larger, and the number of narrow escapes—missionaries forced to flee their homes at a moment's notice to escape bandits or Communists—is even larger still. These figures concern the adventures of missionaries only and do not take into account the numerous piracies on the high seas when foreign officers and passengers have been carried off, or outrages such as the capture of Mrs. Pawley and Mr. Charles Corkran. They do not include attacks and captures made in the C.E.R. area, or the German wireless operator attached to one of the air lines in the far west of this country who vanished. The death of Mr. Riley, "The Times" correspondent who disappeared in Honan, the Linchang outrage, and the Thorburn incident are also outside their scope. And it is possible that some outrages in south China affecting Catholic missionaries and about which it has been difficult to obtain accurate information in Shanghai owing to the fact that their headquarters are in the south, have been omitted.
* * *
It may seem a somewhat morbid subject to dwell upon, and, therefore, the figures are given no more than as a matter of record. Much more interesting are some of the stories of escapes and flights which are occasionally heard. It is a remarkable development that such escapes have become so common that those who have experienced them consider them hardly worthy of mention. The fact remains, however, that most of them are epic stories—of courage, faith, and the most extraordinary loyalty on the part of Chinese friends who stand to lose everything if they are discovered in assisting the foreigner and who might avoid all attention by simply lying low. There is the story of the two British women who were trapped in an inland city while bandits ravaged its streets, committing all sorts of atrocities, pillaging and murdering at will. The bandits knew well that there were two foreign women in the place and they searched high and low without result. Some of the women's Chinese friends had hidden them.

When the search became too hot, they dressed the women in men's clothes and, to disguise their colouring and sex, gave them Balaclava helmets, those woollen contraptions that cover the head and neck and leave only a small part of the face visible. In long Chinese wadded gowns and with these helmets over their heads, the two women were put on to wheelbarrows and wheeled through the streets under the noses of the bandits, out through the gates past bandit guards who were searching everyone, and so to safety after a hazardous flight over frozen roads.
* * *
Some years ago Honan was one of the worst provinces in China for bandits. There were Red Spears, Yellow Spears, and a variety of semi-secret organizations that terrorized the whole area. Those were the days of the civil wars between different generals, when a military commander might be on one side one day and the other the next, and his troops might be soldiers when victorious and bandits when defeated, according to the turn of chance. Whatever they were, the sufferings of the common people were about the same. Protectors extracted as much from them as the outlaws from whom they were protecting them, and the only difference was that they were not killed quite so mercilessly when the soldiers were there. They were robbed just the same. The country people of Honan organized a kind of intelligence system which warned them of the approach of outlaw bands. Then they would flock into the nearest city with their cattle and everything they could take with them, and from its walls watch the lurid glare in the sky which told them that their homesteads were in flames. Along the walls of the cities the inhabitants used to light beacons to show up the approaches. No one was allowed to enter or leave the city without proving his bona fides, as it had sometimes happened that bandits entered the city with the refugees and opened the gates to their comrades outside. If ever there was a reign of terror, in the most dreadful meaning of the term, it was in those days in Honan. The missionaries were withdrawn from the worst parts when the full significance of the situation was realized, but before this happened a number went through the most harrowing experiences.
* * *
There were six major outrages in which foreign missionaries were concerned in Honan province during the month of November, 1923. At the beginning of the month, six thousand bandits attacked and looted the prosperous market town of Chowkiachow, in the south of the province, and carried off six American missionaries. On November 6 a Briton, a member of the China Inland Mission, was seized and carried off by a band that attacked Shangweng-hsien. On November 8 the Rev. Mr. Borg-Breen and his five years old child were carried off from Hsi-hsien. On the same day, the Rev. George Holm was captured at Chengyuang-hsien. On November 13 reports were received that fourteen persons—British, American, French, Belgian, Norwegian, Italian, and Swiss—had been carried off. Of these only three Englishmen escaped and returned safely; the rest are still missing. On November 14 two more missionaries were carried off from Chumatien, after a battle between troops belonging to one of the northern generals and the bandits, in which the troops were routed. Twenty-seven foreigners, including a five years old child: not a bad bag for the bandits in a fortnight!
* * *
To skip a few years, until the bandit menace became known as the Communist menace and there was an intensification of the anti-foreign activities of the outlaws. Up to that time the foreigner had been regarded as a useful person for ransom, but in most cases there had been no hatred of him. Afterwards the Communist movement gave attacks on foreigners a cloak of patriotism and invested anti-Christian actions with a Moscow-made sanctity. The peak of this phase in the movement was the outrage in Nanking in 1927, which resulted in the shelling of certain points in the city by H.M.S. Emerald and the American destroyer Noah. The proscription of the Communists by the Government made things somewhat easier in the Yangtze ports and neighbourhood, and it says a great deal for the efforts of the new government in Nanking that, since then, disorder has been driven into the hinterland. It would be idle, however, to look no further. In Szechuan at present the conditions are every bit as bad as ever they were in the central China provinces some years ago. The government has recognized this and is taking action accordingly.
* * *
Among the more recent outrages two are selected as a matter of record. The one is the capture of the Misses Nettleton and Harrison in Fukien and their subsequent murder, after their captors, described as Communist-bandits, had demanded $5,000 ransom and sent a finger of one of the women as an earnest of their intentions. The other is the capture of Mr. J. H. Ferguson in Anhwei—one of the most wanton and senseless of all the crimes. Mr. Ferguson, whose fate has not yet been accurately ascertained but for whom hope has

被俘记
作者：KUNIKOS

自革命以来，在中国各地约有350名传教士被匪徒劫持。其中，已知约有55人遇害，另有数人的下落至今不明，尽管人们仍抱有一线希望，认为他们之中或许有人能在历经可怕磨难后幸存，但这种希望非常渺茫。抢劫和拦路打劫的案件数量要大得多，而死里逃生的案例——传教士为躲避匪徒或共产党人，不得不瞬间离家出逃——则更是多不胜数。这些数据仅涉及传教士的遭遇，并未计入公海上发生的多起海盗行为，当时外国官员和乘客曾被掳走；也未包括诸如鲍利夫人（Mrs. Pawley）和查尔斯·科克兰先生（Mr. Charles Corkran）被绑架之类的暴行。此外，数据也不包括在中东铁路（C.E.R.）区域发生的袭击和抓捕事件，或者在我国极西部地区某条航空公司任职的一名德国无线电操作员失踪的案件。《泰晤士报》驻河南记者莱利先生（Mr. Riley）的死亡、林昌暴行（Linchang outrage）以及索伯恩事件（Thorburn incident）也不在其统计范围内。而且，华南地区一些针对天主教传教士的暴行可能也被遗漏，由于他们的总部设在南方，上海方面难以获得准确信息。
* * *
沉湎于此话题似乎略显病态，因此列出这些数据仅作为记录。相比之下，偶尔听到的某些逃脱和逃亡的故事要有趣得多。值得注意的是，此类逃脱已变得如此常见，以至于经历过的人甚至认为不值一提。然而事实是，其中大多数都是史诗般的故事——关乎勇气、信仰，以及中国朋友所表现出的非凡忠诚；这些中国朋友若因协助外国人而被发现，将失去一切，而他们本可通过 simply lying low（低调隐匿）来避免所有关注。有这样一则故事：两名英国妇女被困在一座内陆城市，当时匪徒正在街头肆虐，犯下各种暴行，随意掠夺和杀戮。匪徒深知城内有两名外国妇女，于是四处搜捕，却一无所获。原来，这两位妇女的中国朋友将她们藏了起来。

当搜查变得过于紧迫时，她们给这两名妇女换上男装，并给她们戴上巴拉克拉瓦帽（Balaclava helmets，一种覆盖头部和颈部、仅露出面部一小部分的羊毛制品），以掩饰她们的肤色和性别特征。这两名妇女身穿长款中式棉袍，头戴这种帽子，被放在独轮车上，在匪徒的眼皮底下穿过街道，经过正在盘查每个人的匪徒哨卡，走出城门，最终在冰冻的道路上经历了一番危险的逃亡后抵达安全地带。
* * *
几年前，河南是中国匪患最严重的省份之一。那里有红枪会、黄枪会以及各种半秘密组织，恐怖笼罩着整个地区。那是不同军阀之间内战频仍的日子，军事指挥官可能今天属于这一方，明天就倒向另一方，其部队在胜利时是士兵，失败时则沦为匪徒，全凭机缘巧合。无论身份如何变换，百姓所受的苦难大致相同。所谓的保护者从百姓身上榨取的财物，与他们所要保护的百姓免受其害的那些不法之徒所勒索的一样多，唯一的区别是，当士兵在场时，百姓被杀害的程度不那么残忍罢了。他们同样遭到抢劫。河南的乡下人建立了一种类似情报系统的机制，用以警告匪帮的逼近。随后，他们会带着牲畜和所有能带走的东西涌入最近的城市，从城墙上注视着天空中预示家园陷入火海的熊熊红光。沿着城墙，居民们点燃烽火以显示敌情。任何人未经证明其真实身份（bona fides），不得进出城市，因为曾发生过匪徒混入难民进入城内，并为城外的同伙打开城门的情况。如果说真有“恐怖统治”（reign of terror），且是在该词最可怕的意义上，那便是当时河南的情形。当局势的全部严重性被认识到后，传教士们从最危险的地区撤离，但在此之前，许多人经历了极其痛苦的经历。
* * *
1923年11月期间，河南省发生了六起涉及外国传教士的重大暴行。月初，六千名匪徒袭击并洗劫了该省南部繁荣的集镇周家口（Chowkiachow），掳走了六名美国传教士。11月6日，一名内地会（China Inland Mission）的英国成员在上翁县（Shangweng-hsien，音译）遭一伙匪徒袭击并被掳走。11月8日，博格-布林牧师（Rev. Mr. Borg-Breen）及其五岁的孩子从西县（Hsi-hsien，音译）被掳走。同日，乔治·霍尔姆牧师（Rev. George Holm）在成源县（Chengyuang-hsien，音译）被捕。11月13日，收到报告称有十四人被掳走，其中包括英国人、美国人、法国人、比利时人、挪威人、意大利人和瑞士人。其中只有三名英国人逃脱并安全返回；其余人仍下落不明。11月14日，在北方某位将军的部队与匪徒发生战斗且部队被击溃后，又有两名传教士从朱马店（Chumatien，音译）被掳走。两周内共有二十七名外国人（包括一名五岁儿童）被掳：对匪徒来说，这收获可真不小！
* * *
时光飞逝几年，直到匪患被称为共产主义威胁，且不法之徒的反外活动加剧。在此之前，外国人被视为索取赎金的有用对象，但在大多数情况下，人们对他并无仇恨。此后，共产主义运动给攻击外国人的行为披上了爱国主义的外衣，并赋予反基督教行动一种源自莫斯科的神圣性。这一阶段运动的顶峰是1927年的南京暴行，导致英国皇家海军翡翠号（H.M.S. Emerald）和美国驱逐舰诺亚号（Noah）炮击该市某些地点。南京政府取缔共产党后，长江各港口及周边地区的局势有所缓和，这也充分说明了南京新政府的努力，自此以后，混乱被驱赶至内陆地区。然而，若就此止步而不作进一步观察则是徒劳的。目前四川的状况与几年前华中各省的状况一样糟糕。政府已认识到这一点，并正在采取相应行动。
* * *
在近期的暴行中，选取两例作为记录。一例是内特尔顿小姐（Miss Nettleton）和哈里森小姐（Miss Harrison）在福建被俘，随后被谋杀；据称俘虏她们的是“共产匪徒”，她们曾索要5,000美元赎金，并寄来其中一名女子的一根手指以表明其意图。另一例是J. H. 弗格森先生（Mr. J. H. Ferguson）在安徽被俘——这是所有罪行中最肆意妄为且毫无意义的一起。弗格森先生的命运尚未确切查明，但人们对他的生还希望

been given up, was an old man
who had devoted the whole of his
life to helping the Chinese people.
A missionary, he had been of
great assistance in distributing
famine relief money to the starv-
ing people in the Hwai River
basin. When he discovered that
the rapacious landlords of the dis-
trict were watching him and
descending upon the unfortunate
peasants to whom he gave relief
and forcing them to disgorge the
few cents he had handed to them
against their arrears in rent, Mr.
Ferguson made his rounds at
night and in secret. He would
leave a few silver pieces conceal-
ed on a doorstep so that the bene-
ficiary could see them when he
opened the door in the morning
and no one would be the wiser.
When he was marched out of the
city of Chengyangkuan crowds
knelt in the streets in the path of
his captors and pleaded that he
should not be taken away. When
they had been trodden down, they
organized a procession of women
to march after the Communists
and pray for Mr. Ferguson's re-
lease. It was all futile. The Reds
took Mr. Ferguson with them
wherever they went, standing him
on platforms for the amusement of
the populace. Mr. Ferguson made
the best of his opportunity and
preached to the crowds that were
there to laugh at him. Surely as
sublime an example of Christian
heroism it is possible to imagine!
page_data.zh: 已经破灭，他是一位老人，毕生致力于帮助中国人民。作为一名传教士，他在向淮河流域的饥民分发赈灾款项方面提供了巨大帮助。当他发现该地区贪婪的地主正在监视他，并降临到接受他救济的不幸农民身上，强迫他们吐出他为了抵偿欠租而交给他们的几分钱时，弗格森先生开始在夜间秘密巡视。他会将几块银元藏在门阶上，以便受助者在早晨开门时能看到，而其他人则不会察觉。当他被押出正阳关（Chengyangkuan）城时，人群跪在他 captors（捕获者/押送者）行进路线的街道上，恳求不要将他带走。当这些人被践踏后，她们组织了一支妇女队伍，跟随在共产党人身后游行，祈祷弗格森先生获释。但这都是徒劳的。红军带着弗格森先生四处移动，将他站在台上供民众取乐。弗格森先生充分利用了这一机会，向那些前来嘲笑他的群众布道。这无疑是人们所能想象到的基督教英雄主义的最崇高典范！

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 16, 1934

STAMS' INFANT DAUGHTER
ESCAPES PARENTS' FATE

Recovered and Taken to Wuhu Mission: Victims'
Terrible Thirty Mile Forced March

LAST LETTERS OF GALLANT MISSIONARY

Ransom Could Not Have Been Paid in Any Cir-
cumstances: "None Would Then Be Safe"

IT was ascertained yesterday by officials of the China Inland Mission
here that Helen, the three-months-old daughter of the Rev. and
Mrs. J. C. Stam, escaped the horrible fate that befell the missionary
couple. At the same time, it was learned how the three were captured,
forced to travel thirty miles over narrow and almost impassable roads,
and held for $20,000 ransom.

The infant has been found and is being returned to Wuhu by Mr.
George Birch, a missionary stationed at Suenscheng, the message
stated. No other details were mentioned, except the bare fact that the
bodies of Mr. and Mrs. Stam are being carried to Wuhu in coffins on
the same highway over which they were led by Communist-bandits
only a few days ago.

The Stams were murdered and the infant abandoned when aid was
close at hand, Mission officials surmise, because Mr. Birch set out in
search, taking with him provisions and other aid, soon after the bandits
swooped down upon Tsingteh, burned the Yamen, and wrecked the
town.

JUST TOO LATE TO EFFECT ESCAPE

How the missionaries were cap-
tured is revealed for the first time in
letters written by the Rev. John
Stam, himself, and sent to his friend
and director the Rev. G. W. Gibb,
of the China Inland Mission head-
quarters here. Two letters, one
written on December 6, the day of
the capture, and the other the fol-
lowing day, were received here in
the Friday and Saturday mail de-
liveries.

Missionary's Last Words

Possibly the last words written by
this brave missionary, who went to
his death courageously, were those
closing the second letter to Mr. Gibb.
After describing his futile attempts
to prevail upon the Communists to
release his wife and their infant Mr.
Stam ended:-
"God give you wisdom in what to
do, and give us grace and fortitude.
He is able."
This letter, dated December 7, and
written in Miaochiao, was entrusted
to a Christian Chinese and carried
to Kinghsien, where it was posted
on December 12. In this letter, Mr.
Stam tells of the tortuous trip of 30
li, or about thirty miles, in the hands
of the Communists. He tells how
Mrs. Stam was allowed to traverse
a portion of the road riding a horse.
He tells also how the Communists
robbed them of their money, personal
effects, and the money sent by the
mission for distribution as relief for
famine sufferers.

"Just Too Late"

A ransom of $20,000 was placed
upon their heads, Mr. Stam stated in
both messages which reached their
friends, three days or more after
they had been murdered. Details of
the capture were told briefly in the
first letter. Things happened so
suddenly and the bandits fell upon
the town so quickly that the Stams
were not prepared to leave. "We
were just too late," Mr. Stam wrote.
Doubtless with a premonition that
death was soon to come, and fearing
he knew not what he, his wife, and
the three-months-old baby might
suffer at the hands of the Com-
munists, the missionary brought his
first letter to a close with this
prayer:-
"May God be glorified, whether by
life or by death."
The letters are being sent on by
Mr. Gibb to Dr. and Mrs. C. E. Scott,
of the American Presbyterian Mis-
sion, at present in Tsinan, the
capital of Shantung province. They
are the parents of Mrs. Stam.

An Impossible Ransom

According to Mr. Gibb, more com-
plete details concerning the rescue
of the baby are expected to reach
here within the next few days,
possibly when Mr. Birch returns to

斯塔姆（Stam）的幼女
幸免父母厄运

已被寻回并送往芜湖传教站：受害者遭受
可怕的三十英里强行军

英勇传教士的绝笔信

在任何情况下都不可能支付赎金：“否则无人能保安全”

昨日，内地会（China Inland Mission）驻沪官员查明，约翰·C·斯塔姆（J. C. Stam）牧师夫妇三个月大的女儿海伦（Helen），幸免于那对传教士夫妇所遭遇的可怕命运。与此同时，人们也获悉了这三人是如何被俘，如何在狭窄且几乎无法通行的道路上被强迫行进三十英里，以及被索要两万美元赎金的经过。

据消息指出，婴儿已被找到，正由驻扎在宣城的传教士乔治·伯奇（George Birch）先生送回芜湖。除了一具简单的事实——即斯塔姆夫妇的遗体正装在棺材里，沿着几天前他们被共产党匪徒押解走过的同一条公路运往芜湖——之外，未提及更多细节。

传教站官员推测，斯塔姆夫妇遇害、婴儿被遗弃时，救援已近在咫尺，因为伯奇先生在匪徒突袭泾县、焚烧衙门并破坏城镇后不久，便携带给养和其他援助物资出发搜寻。

逃脱仅差一步

传教士如何被俘的细节，首次通过约翰·斯塔姆牧师本人写给其朋友兼上司、内地会驻沪总部主任G. W. 吉布（G. W. Gibb）牧师的信件中披露。两封信，一封写于被俘当日12月6日，另一封写于次日，随周五和周六的邮件送达此处。

传教士的遗言

这位勇敢赴死的传教士留下的最后文字，可能是他致吉布先生第二封信的结尾。在描述了他试图说服共产党人释放其妻子和婴儿但未果后，斯塔姆先生写道：
“愿上帝赐你智慧以知所当行，并赐我们恩典与刚毅。祂是有能的。”
这封信落款日期为12月7日，写于庙首（Miaochiao），托付给一位中国基督徒带至旌德（Kinghsien），并于12月12日寄出。在这封信中，斯塔姆先生讲述了在共产党人控制下曲折行进30里（约三十英里）的经历。他提到斯塔姆夫人曾被允许骑马走过部分路程。他还提到共产党人抢走了他们的钱财、个人物品以及传教站拨发用于救济灾民的款项。

“仅差一步”

斯塔姆先生在两份讯息中均称，匪徒索要两万美元赎金，而这些讯息在他们遇害三天或更久后才送达其朋友手中。第一封信简要叙述了被俘经过。事发如此突然，匪徒攻入城镇如此迅速，以致斯塔姆夫妇来不及撤离。“我们仅差一步，”斯塔姆先生写道。无疑怀着死亡即将来临的预感，并因不知自己、妻子及三个月大的婴儿将在共产党人手中遭受何种苦难而恐惧，这位传教士在第一封信的末尾以如下祷告作结：
“无论生或死，愿上帝得荣耀。”

这些信件正由吉布先生转寄给目前在山东省省会济南的美国长老会（American Presbyterian Mission）的C. E. 斯科特（C. E. Scott）博士夫妇。他们是斯塔姆夫人的父母。

不可能支付的赎金

据吉布先生称，关于婴儿获救的更完整细节预计将在未来几天内送达此处，可能是在伯奇先生返回时。

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 15, 1934

FOR THEIR FAITH
The deaths of Mr. and Mrs.
Stam and their small child
have shocked public opinion
and have evoked the deepest
sympathy for the bereaved families.
Mr. and Mrs. Stam took risks which
pioneers have always taken. Their
untimely end, so far as can be
judged, was due to sheer ill-fortune
in their encountering a small band
of desperate men, fugitives from the
dispersal of the Communist con-
centration in Kiangsi. Whether the
perpetrators will be rounded up and
made to pay the penalty of their
crime remains to be seen. No doubt
the local authorities will do all that
is in their power to bring that to
pass. Meanwhile, to the long record
of missionary martyrs, fresh names
have been added. The thought will
be proudly cherished by the workers
in the field. It illustrates the fervour
of the spirit which, from time im-
memorial, has stimulated the mis-
sionary of whatever faith to minister
in the cause of religion.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1934年12月15日，星期六

为信仰殉道
斯塔姆夫妇及其幼子的死讯震惊舆论，并引起对丧亲家属的最深切同情。斯塔姆夫妇承担了先驱者一贯承担的风险。就所能判断而言，他们的英年早逝纯属不幸，因为他们遭遇了一小群亡命之徒，这些人是江西共产党集中力量被击溃后的逃窜者。肇事者是否会被捕归案并为其罪行受到惩罚，尚待观察。毫无疑问，地方当局将尽其所能促成此事。与此同时，传教士殉道者的长长名单上又增添了新的名字。这一念头将被前线工作人员引以为豪地珍视。它说明了那种自古以来激励着各种信仰的传教士投身宗教事业的精神热忱。

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY. DECEMBER 14, 1934

MURDER OF AMERICANS
BY COMMUNISTS

Mr. Stam, Captured Missionary, Found Dead, with
Body Believed to Be His Baby

NO REFERENCE TO MRS. STAM

Consulate Takes Speedy Action but Effort is
Too Late: Governor Reports Tragedy

THE bodies of two of the three foreign captives taken by Communist-bandits in their raid on the southern Anhwei town of Tsingteh have been discovered near a highway leading out of the city, according to a message received in Shanghai yesterday. The message gave no details, merely stating:—

"Governor reports bodies John Betty Stam found Miaochiao."

Miaochiao is on about six or eight miles from Tsingteh, the city in which the American missionaries were captured, after they had returned to it from Wuhu on the assurance of local officials that the district was safe.

DASTARDLY ACT OF STRAY BAND

Mr. and Mrs. Stam and their infant were captured about December 10. Mr. Stam is a native of Paterson, New Jersey, and Mrs. Stam is the daughter of Dr. and Mrs. C. E. Scott, of the American Presbyterian Mission, who are at present stationed in Tsinan, the capital of Shantung province. Mr. Stam arrived in China in 1929, and Mrs. Stam returned here one year earlier.

Owing to lack of details concerning the capture, it was uncertain last night whether the Betty Stam mentioned in the message referred to Mrs. Stam or to Mr. and Mrs. Stam's 2½ months old infant daughter who was captured at the same time as the missionary couple. It was feared, however, that the message referred to the child, and that there was no danger of capture or attack by Communists. On this assurance, Mr. Stam had returned to Wuhu and brought his wife to the centre of their life-work. Very shortly afterwards, the bandits descended on the town and took them captive.

Details of the outrage have not yet been received in Shanghai. It is surmised, however, that the captors are one of those stray bands of Communists who have been driven over the Kiangsi border as a result of the campaign initiated and carried through by Gen. Chiang Kai-shek. So many small and apparently harmless bands have been dispersed by this drive—bands that live by raiding cities which hitherto have been regarded as safe and are, therefore, not so strongly fortified or prepared as those more directly in touch with the danger-zone—that observers consider it quite understandable that the local authorities should regard themselves as outside the sphere of Communist attack.

[Map labels: N, S, WUHU, ANKING, YANGTZE, ANHWEI, TSINGTEH, CHEKIANG]

Mrs. Stam, who has been in poor health throughout the summer, still remains in the bandits' hands.

Mr. and Mrs. Stam, comparatively recent arrivals in the mission field in China, had only returned to their station at Tsingteh after investigations by Mr. Stam and a colleague whether the district was safe. Owing to Mrs. Stam's health and the age of the infant, they had spent most of the summer months in Wuhu. Before returning to Tsingteh, Mr. Stam personally had visited the district and had been assured by local officials
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1934年12月14日，星期五

美国人遭共产党人杀害

被俘传教士斯塔姆先生被发现身亡，身旁有一具被认为是其婴儿的尸体

未提及斯塔姆夫人

领事馆迅速采取行动但为时已晚：省长报告悲剧

据昨日上海收到的一则消息，在安徽南部泾县城被共产党匪徒袭击时被捕的三名外籍人质中，有两人的尸体在通往城外的一条公路附近被发现。该消息未提供细节，仅称：—

“省长报告，约翰（John）、贝蒂·斯塔姆（Betty Stam）的尸体在庙首（Miaochiao）被发现。”

庙首距离泾县约六至八英里，美国传教士正是在此地被俘，此前他们曾从芜湖返回此处，因为地方官员保证该地区是安全的。

流窜匪帮的卑劣行径

斯塔姆夫妇及其婴儿大约在12月10日被俘。斯塔姆先生是新泽西州帕特森（Paterson）人，斯塔姆夫人是美国长老会传教士C. E. 斯科特博士夫妇的女儿，斯科特夫妇目前驻扎在山东省省会济南。斯塔姆先生于1929年来华，斯塔姆夫人则早一年回到此处。

由于缺乏关于被俘的详细情况，昨晚尚不确定消息中提到的“贝蒂·斯塔姆”是指斯塔姆夫人，还是指与传教士夫妇同时被俘的他们两个半月大的女婴。然而，人们担心消息指的是孩子，并且认为不存在被共产党人俘虏或攻击的危险。基于这一保证，斯塔姆先生返回芜湖，并将妻子带到他们生活工作的中心。不久之后，匪徒袭击该镇并将他们俘虏。

上海尚未收到关于此次暴行的详细情况。不过，据推测，绑架者是那些因蒋介石将军发起并实施的围剿行动而被赶过江西边界的共产党流窜股匪之一。此次行动驱散了众多看似无害的小股匪帮——这些匪帮靠劫掠迄今被视为安全、因此防御工事或备战程度不如直接处于危险区的那些城镇为生——观察家认为，地方当局认为自己处于共产党攻击范围之外，这是完全可以理解的。

[地图标注：北，南，芜湖，安庆，长江，安徽，泾县，浙江]

整个夏季健康状况不佳的斯塔姆夫人，仍留在匪徒手中。

斯塔姆夫妇是相对较新加入在华传教领域的成员，在斯塔姆先生和一位同事调查该地区是否安全后，他们才刚刚返回泾县的驻地。由于斯塔姆夫人的健康和婴儿的年龄，他们夏季的大部分时间都在芜湖度过。在返回泾县之前，斯塔姆先生亲自视察了该地区，并得到地方官员的保证

page_data.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 12, 1934

REDS CAPTURE
AMERICANS

Man, Wife, and Infant
Seized in Anhwei

ROVERS FROM KIANGSI

Missionaries Told That
District Was Safe

SPECIAL TO THE "N.C.D.N."

Mr. and Mrs. J. C. Stam and their two and a half months' old daughter have been captured by Communists at Tsingteh in southern Anhwei, according to messages received in Shanghai on Monday and confirmed yesterday. Mr. and Mrs. Stam are comparatively newly joined members of the China Inland Mission and only recently returned to their station at Tsingteh on the assurance of local officials that the district was safe. More than usual anxiety is being felt in mission circles over the capture, owing to the knowledge that Mrs. Stam has not been in good health and that she will have the burden of an infant in arms.

Mr. Stam is a native of New Jersey and Mrs. Stam is the daughter of Dr. and Mrs. C. E. Scott of the American Presbyterian Mission in Tsinan, Shantung. No details of the capture had been received here yesterday.

Owing to the disorder in their district and to Mrs. Stam's health, the family had been spending the summer in Wuhu. A short while ago, however, Mr. Stam and a colleague revisited the district in order to see conditions for themselves. While they were there they were officially assured that there was no danger, so Mr. Stam returned to Wuhu and brought Mrs. Stam and their infant back with them. They had not been back long before they were captured.

Head by Roving Outlaws

It is believed that their captors are one of the bands of Communists that have been scattered by the Anti-Red drive in Kiangsi and have still to be rounded up by the Government troops. Several bands of these roving outlaws are reported to have crossed the border in Anhwei where they have been terrorizing the local people.

Immediately upon receipt of news of the capture the matter was put into the hands of the American Legation. In the meantime Mr. W. J. Hanna, the China Inlands Mission superintendent for Anhwei who has been in Shanghai attending the mission's council meetings, is leaving for the district in an attempt to make contact with the captives or their captors.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1934年12月12日，星期三

赤匪俘虏
美国人

男子、妻子和婴儿
在安徽被劫

来自江西的流寇

传教士被告知
该地区安全

《字林西报》专电

据周一收到并于昨日证实的消息，J. C. 斯塔姆夫妇及其两个半月大的女儿在安徽南部泾县被共产党人俘虏。斯塔姆夫妇是内地会相对较新的成员，近期才在地方官员保证该地区安全的情况下返回泾县驻地。鉴于已知斯塔姆夫人健康状况不佳，且需怀抱婴儿，传教界对被俘一事感到比平时更多的焦虑。

斯塔姆先生是新泽西州人，斯塔姆夫人是山东济南美国长老会传教士C. E. 斯科特博士夫妇的女儿。截至昨日，此处尚未收到关于被俘的任何细节。

由于所在地区的混乱以及斯塔姆夫人的健康状况，这家人整个夏天都在芜湖度过。然而，不久前，斯塔姆先生和一位同事重新视察该地区，以亲自了解情况。在那里期间，他们得到官方保证称没有危险，因此斯塔姆先生返回芜湖，接回了斯塔姆夫人和他们的婴儿。他们回去不久便被俘。

头目为流窜不法之徒

据信，绑架他们的是在江西“剿赤”行动中被击散、尚待政府军围歼的共产党股匪之一。据报道，几股此类流窜匪徒已越过边界进入安徽，在当地恐吓百姓。

一收到被俘消息，此事即交由美国公使馆处理。与此同时，一直在此参加传教站理事会会议的内地会安徽区监督W. J. 汉纳（W. J. Hanna）先生正启程前往该地区，试图与被俘者或其绑架者取得联系。

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 16, 1934

Troops In Hot
Pursuit After
Stam Killers

Baby Helen Found To
Be Safe; Kohfields
Escape To Suancheng

Yesterday morning the local offices of the China Inland Mission learned that Helen Priscilla Stam, three-months' old daughter of Mr. and Mrs. John Stam, who were murdered by bandits after their capture at Tsingteh, Anhwei, had been brought to Wuhu by Mr. George A. Birch of the China Inland Mission who is stationed at Suancheng, Anhwei, near Tsingteh.
According to other reports received here, Mr. and Mrs. E. A. Kohfield, Americans, stationed by the China Inland Mission at Tungki, have escaped with their three children from Tungki to Suancheng.

Chinese reports state that a horde of about 3,000 bandits, among them believed to be the murderers of Mr. and Mrs. Stam, are being hotly pursued by 10,000 government and provincial troops.

Stam Baby Believed Safe
PEIPING, Dec. 15.—(Reuters)—Helen Stam, the three-months old baby of Mr. and Mrs. C. J. Stam, American missionaries who were killed on December 8 at Miaochiao, 20 miles from their station at Tsingteh, is reported safe at Wuhu.
The report is contained in a telegram received by the United States Legation today from Nan-king.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》，1934年12月16日，星期日

军队紧追
斯塔姆案凶手

婴儿海伦被发现
安然无恙；科菲尔德
一家逃至宣城

昨日上午，内地会当地办事处获悉，约翰·斯塔姆夫妇在安徽泾县被俘后被匪徒杀害，他们三个月大的女儿海伦·普里西拉·斯塔姆（Helen Priscilla Stam）已由驻扎在安徽泾县附近宣城的内地会传教士乔治·A·伯奇（George A. Birch）先生带至芜湖。
根据此处收到的其他报告，由内地会派驻桐城（Tungki）的美国人E. A·科菲尔德（E. A. Kohfield）夫妇已携三名子女从桐城逃至宣城。

中方报道称，一股约3000人的匪帮（其中包括被认为杀害斯塔姆夫妇的凶手）正受到一万名政府军和省军的猛烈追击。

斯塔姆婴儿据信安全
北平，12月15日电（路透社）——据报道，海伦·斯塔姆（Helen Stam），即12月8日在距其泾县驻地20英里的庙首被杀的美国传教士C. J. 斯塔姆夫妇三个月大的婴儿，在芜湖安然无恙。
此消息包含在美国公使馆今日从南京收到的一份电报中。

page_data.en:
HE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 15, 1

Stams Died
In Battle,
Probe Shows

Couple Found Dead At
Finish Of Engagement
Between Bandits And
Troops Of Government

Fate Of Child Is Yet
Unknown; Little Hope
Held Out For Safety

NANKING, Dec. 14.—(Reuters).
—The tragic story of the capture
and death of the two American
missionaries, Mr. and Mrs. C. J.
Stam, was brought to light today,
although the fate of their infant
daughter, Helen, is still unknown.
On December 12 about 3,000 com-
munists made a surprise attack on
Tsingteh, about 120 miles south
of Nanking, where Mr. and Mrs.
Stam were stationed, and captured
the city.
After looting the town the com-
munists left the next day carrying
with them 10 persons among whom
were Mr. and Mrs. Stam and their
baby. They proceeded with their
victims in a southwest direction
towards the mountains from where
they had come.
Government troops, however,
overtook them at Miaochiao, 50 li
from Tsingteh, where a severe eng-
agement took place. Later among
the dead on the battlefield govern-
ment troops found the two bodies
which were believed to be those of
Mr. and Mrs. Stam.

Although the body of their three-
months-old daughter has not been
found, little hope is held out for
her safety.
Meanwhile, United States auth-
orities in China acting under in-
structions from Washington, have
renewed their representations to
the Nanking and provincial auth-
orities for vigorous measures to be
taken to rescue the child if she is
still alive.
It is reported from Wuhu that
Fr. W. J. Hanna, superintendent of
the China Inland Mission there, left
today for Miaochiao to bring the
bodies of Mr. and Mrs. Stam to
Wuhu for identification and burial.
Another foreign missionary in
Tsingteh, believed to be a Spanish
Catholic priest, happened to be out
of town at the time and thus had
a lucky escape from capture.

Officials Investigating Murder
NANKING, Dec. 14.—(Reuters).—
An investigation into the murder
by communist-bandits of Mr. and
Mrs. John Stam, American mission-
aries, whose bodies were discovered
yesterday near the southern Anhui
town of Tsingteh, is being carried
out by Mr. Willys R. Peck, American
consul-general here, and Mr. Dou-
glas Jenkins, Jr., vice-consul.
The American consular officials
left for Wuhu last night following
the receipt by the Foreign Office
of a telegram from General Liu
Chen-hwa governor of the Anhui
Provincial Government, announcing
the discovery of the bodies of the
slain missionaries.
The purpose of their trip is to
collect information regarding the
capture and subsequent murder of
the missionary couple. Mr. Jenkins
is expected to return here today.
Mr. and Mrs. Stam, who were
connected with the China Inland
Mission, were captured by com-
munist-bandits on December 6
while en route to their station at
Tsingteh from Wuhu.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，星期六，12月15日，1

斯坦姆夫妇
战死，
调查显示

一对夫妇在匪徒与
政府军交火结束时
被发现死亡

幼童下落仍不明；
生还希望渺茫

南京，12月14日.—（路透社）.
—两名美国传教士斯坦姆先生和夫人（Mr. and Mrs. C. J. Stam）被俘并遇害的悲惨故事今日真相大白，尽管他们幼女海伦（Helen）的下落仍然未知。12月12日，约3,000名共产党人突袭了位于南京以南约120英里的青弋江（Tsingteh），斯坦姆夫妇即驻守于此，该城随即陷落。
共产党人在洗劫城镇后于次日离开，带走了10人，其中包括斯坦姆夫妇及其婴儿。他们挟持受害者向西南方向的山地进发，那是他们来的地方。
然而，政府军在距离青弋江50里的庙桥（Miaochiao）追上了他们，双方发生了激烈交战。随后，政府军在战场上的死者中发现了两具尸体，据信是斯坦姆先生和夫人的遗体。

虽然他们三个月大的女儿的尸体尚未找到，但对其安全的希望十分渺茫。
与此同时，在华美国当局根据华盛顿的指示，再次向南京及省级当局提出交涉，要求采取有力措施，若孩子尚在人世，务必将其救出。
据芜湖消息，当地中国内地会（China Inland Mission）总监W. J. 汉纳神父（Fr. W. J. Hanna）今日启程前往庙桥，将斯坦姆夫妇的遗体运至芜湖进行辨认和安葬。
青弋江的另一名外籍传教士，据信是一名西班牙天主教神父，事发时恰好不在城内，因此幸运地逃脱了被俘的命运。

官员调查谋杀案
南京，12月14日.—（路透社）.—
针对共产党匪徒谋杀美国传教士约翰·斯坦姆（John Stam）夫妇一案的调查正在进行中，两人的尸体昨日在安徽南部青弋江镇附近被发现。负责调查的是美国驻此地总领事威利斯·R·佩克（Willys R. Peck）先生和副领事小道格拉斯·詹金斯（Douglas Jenkins, Jr.）先生。
在美国外交部收到安徽省政府主席刘镇华（Liu Chen-hwa）将军宣布发现遇害传教士尸体的电报后，美国领事官员于昨晚启程前往芜湖。
此行的目的是收集有关这对传教士夫妇被俘及随后被杀的信息。预计詹金斯先生将于今日返回此处。
斯坦姆夫妇隶属于中国内地会，于12月6日在从芜湖前往其驻地青弋江的途中被共产党匪徒俘虏。

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 14,

Stams Killed
By Bandits
At Miaochiao

Anhwei Governor Tells
Hanna Bodies Of Two
Persons Found; Fate
Of Third Unrevealed

Death Follows After 2
American Missionaries
Captured At Tsingteh

Two of the three Stams, father,
mother and baby daughter,
have been murdered by the bandits
who captured them at Tsingteh,
South Anhwei, recently. The two
are thought by local missionary cir-
cles to be Rev. C. J. Stam and his
baby daughter, Betty. The fate of
Mrs. Stam is unknown.

A telegram was received from
Superintendent W. J. Hanna of the
China Inland Mission from Wuhu
yesterday afternoon stating "gov-
ernor reports bodies of John and
Betty Stam found at Miaochiao."
Mr. Hanna left Shanghai early this
week for Wuhu with the intention
of making a contact with the
bandits.

With reports of the death of the
Stams, news reached here yesterday
expressing the fear that Rev. and
Mrs. E. A. Kohfield, American mis-
sionaries who are stationed at Tunki,
South Anhwei, not far from Tsing-
teh, have also been captured by
bandits. The reports could not be
confirmed. The couple has three
children.

Further details of the Stam tragedy
could not be learned last night. It
is expected that Mr. Hanna will
leave for southern Anhwei in an
effort to locate the bodies of the
two missionaries as well as to as-
certain the fate of the child.

Word of the capture was first
brought out by the servant of the
Stams in Tsingteh. Mr. Willis R.
Peck, counsellor of the American
Legation resident in Nanking, called
in the Foreign Office Wednesday
morning and confirmed the report
of the capture. He also urged
that all possible steps be taken by
the government for the release of
the captives.

Mr. and Mrs. Stam are compara-
tively new to the China Inland
Mission, having joined the organiza-
tion only a short time ago. They
left for their station in Tsingteh,
which is about 120 miles south of
Nanking, several weeks ago. Mr.
Stam is a native of New Jersey and
Mrs. Stam is the daughter of Dr.
and Mrs. C. E. Scott of the
American Presbyterian Mission in
Tsinan, Shantung.

It is believed that their captors
are one of the bands of Communists
that have been scattered by the
anti-Red drive in Kiangsi and have
still to be rounded up by the gov-
ernment troops. Several bands of
these roving outlaws are reported
to have crossed the border in
Anhui where they have been ter-
rorizing the villages.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，星期五，12月14日，

斯坦姆夫妇
在庙桥
被匪徒杀害

安徽省长告知汉纳
发现两人尸体；
第三人下落未明

两名美国传教士
在青弋江被俘后
遇害

斯坦姆一家三人——父亲、母亲和幼女——中，有两人已被最近在安徽南部青弋江将他们俘虏的匪徒杀害。当地传教界人士认为这两人是C. J. 斯坦姆牧师和他的幼女贝蒂（Betty）。斯坦姆夫人的下落不明。

昨天下午收到来自中国内地会芜湖区总监W. J. 汉纳的电报，称“省长报告在庙桥发现约翰和贝蒂·斯坦姆的尸体”。汉纳先生本周早些时候离开上海前往芜湖，意图与匪徒取得联系。

随着斯坦姆夫妇死讯的传播，昨日有消息传到此处，表达了对驻扎在安徽南部屯溪（Tunki，距青弋江不远）的美国传教士E. A. 科菲尔德（E. A. Kohfield）牧师夫妇也被匪徒俘虏的担忧。这些报道未能得到证实。这对夫妇有三个孩子。

昨晚无法获悉关于斯坦姆悲剧的更多细节。预计汉纳先生将前往安徽南部，试图找到这两名传教士的尸体，并查明孩子的下落。

关于被俘的消息最初是由斯坦姆家在青弋江的仆人传出的。常驻南京的美国公使馆参赞威利斯·R·佩克（Willis R. Peck）先生于周三上午拜访外交部，确认了被俘的报告。他还敦促政府采取一切可能步骤释放人质。

斯坦姆夫妇加入中国内地会的时间相对较短，不久前才加入该组织。几周前，他们前往位于南京以南约120英里的青弋江驻地。斯坦姆先生是新泽西州人，斯坦姆夫人是山东济南美国长老会传教团C. E. 斯科特（C. E. Scott）博士夫妇的女儿。

据信，绑架他们的是在江西“剿赤”行动中被击散、尚未被政府军彻底肃清的一股共产党匪帮。据报道，这几股流窜匪徒已越过边界进入安徽，并在当地村庄制造恐怖。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, December 15, 1934

Baby Of Stams
Reported Safe

China Inland Mission
Receives Assurance
From Wuhu

"The Stam baby is safe" was the brief report from Wuhu received by the China Inland Mission here this morning.

Sympathy Expressed
(United Press)
WASHINGTON, Dec. 14.—D'Alfre Sze-kai Soong, Chinese Minister to Washington today sent a letter to the families of the Rev. Mr. John Stam and his wife, expressing profound sympathy over their murder by Communist bandits in Anhwei Province, China.

Dr. Soong said that he knew the sorrow of the bereaved families was shared by many Chinese, who considered the missionaries amongst their best friends.

Details Of Incident
(By Post Correspondent)
WUHU, Dec. 13.—The deaths of Rev. John C. and Mrs. Stam of the China Inland Mission at Tsingteh, Anhwei, have been reported through the Superintendent of the Anhwei Mission, Rev. W. J. Hanna, of Wuhu. Mr. Hanna received the news in a telegram through the local magistrate from Governor Liu Chen-huan, who is conducting his bandit suppression campaign from headquarters in Chihleh. General Uu reported that the military at Miao Shou, twenty miles from Tsingteh, have discovered the bodies of Mr. and Mrs. Stam. The telegram further states that no trace of the three months old Helen Priscilla has been found. The troops are following the bandits in close pursuit.

Missionaries Evacuate
It is not known how large the band of communists is that looted Tsing-teh, nor whether they are outright communists or bandits recruited from the draught sufferers of the last summer. Reports from the south of the province have been increasingly disquieting during the last few weeks, and missionary families are evacuating.

Mr. Howard Smith and family of Nanling, who had such harrowing experiences in Szachuen, have arrived in Wuhu, and others are on their way here from Tunki, Lanchi, and Ching Hsien. The center of the disturbance seems to be in the vicinity of the famous Yellow Mountains (Hwang Shan) some miles north of the inter-provincial motor highway that connects Nanking with Nanchang.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与美商日报》，1934年12月15日，星期六

据报道斯坦姆
婴儿安然无恙

中国内地会
收到来自芜湖的
保证

“斯坦姆婴儿安全”是今早中国内地会在此处收到的来自芜湖的简短报告。

表示同情
（合众社）
华盛顿，12月14日.—中国驻华盛顿公使宋子凯（D'Alfre Sze-kai Soong，音译，注：应为宋子良或相关外交人员，原文如此）今日致信约翰·斯坦姆牧师及其夫人的家属，对他们在中国安徽省被共产党匪徒谋杀表示深切同情。

宋博士说，他知道许多中国人也分担着丧亲家庭的悲痛，他们认为传教士是他们最好的朋友。

事件详情
（本报通讯员）
芜湖，12月13日.—中国内地会安徽区总监、驻芜湖的W. J. 汉纳牧师报告了该会约翰·C·斯坦姆牧师及夫人在安徽青弋江遇害的消息。汉纳先生通过当地县长收到了来自刘镇华省长的电报，刘省长正在池河（Chihleh，音译）总部指挥剿匪行动。刘将军报告称，军队在距离青弋江二十里的庙首（Miao Shou，音译，前文为Miaochiao）发现了斯坦姆先生和夫人的尸体。电报还指出，尚未发现三个月大的海伦·普里西拉（Helen Priscilla）的踪迹。部队正在紧密追击匪徒。

传教士撤离
目前尚不清楚洗劫青弋江的共产党匪帮规模有多大，也不清楚他们是纯粹的共产党人，还是去年夏季从灾民中招募的匪徒。过去几周，来自该省南部的报告越来越令人不安，传教士家庭正在撤离。

在南陵（Nanling）有着如此痛苦经历的霍华德·史密斯（Howard Smith）先生及其家人已抵达芜湖，其他人正从屯溪（Tunki）、兰溪（Lanchi，音译）和泾县（Ching Hsien，音译）赶来。骚乱中心似乎位于著名的黄山（Hwang Shan）附近，那里位于连接南京和南昌的省际公路以北数英里处。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, December 14, 1934

Bandits In Anhwei
Slay Missionaries

Two Americans Die As
Result Of Raid At
Tsingteh City

Confirmation of news of the
death of Mr. John Stam and pos-
sibly of his wife, American mis-
sionaries who were captured by
bandits December 10 in a raid on
Tsingteh, a town in southern An-
hwei, has been received in Shang-
hai by the China Inland Mission in
the form of a terse telegraphic
message stating that their bodies
have been found at Miaochiao, about
seven miles from Tsingteh.

Owing to lack of details, since
the telegram merely read: "Gov-
ernor reports bodies John Betty
Stam found Miaochiao"—there is
uncertainty as to whether the Betty
Stam mentioned is Mrs. Stam or
her infant daughter of 2-1/2 months
who was captured with her parents
on December 10.

Recent Arrivals

Mr. and Mrs. Stam were com-
paratively recent arrivals in the
mission field and returned recently
to their station at Tsingteh after
they had received official assurances
that it would be safe to do so. But
within a brief space after their re-
turn bandits swooped down on the
town and carried them into captiv-
ity.

Mr. Stam is a native of Paterson,
New Jersey. Mrs. Stam is the
daughter of Dr. and Mrs. C. E.
Scott of the American Presbyterian
Mission, who are at present station-
ed in Tsinan.

Murderers Sought
(United Press)

WASHINGTON, Dec. 13.—Con-
fidence that the Chinese National
Government and the authorities of
Anhwei Province would make every
effort to apprehend the murderers
of Rev. and Mrs. John Stam was
expressed today by Under-Secre-
tary of State William Phillips III.

The slain bodies of Mr. and Mrs.
Stam were found at Miaochiao,
about 10 miles from Tsingteh, in
southern Anhwei Province where
the American missionaries were
captured by a group of bandits be-
lieved to be Communists. The
fate of their four-month-old child
who was also kidnapped has not yet
been ascertained.

New In Field

The couple were attached to the
China Inland Mission station in
Tsingteh and had not long been in
the missionary field. Rev. Stam
was a native of Paterson, New Jer-
sey, and Mrs. Stam was born in
China although she attended
Wheaton College, near Chicago.

Mrs. Elizabeth Scott Stam, who
was known as "Betty" among her
friends, was the daughter of Dr.
and Mrs. C. E. Scott of the Amer-
ican Presbyterian Mission at Tsi-
nan, Shantung.

Escape Cut Off

According to a letter received by
the China Inland Mission head-
quarters in Shanghai written by
Rev. Stam after their capture by
Communists, they had no time to
escape as the Red attack was sud-
den and unexpected. Their cap-
tors, the letter said, were demand-
ing U.S.$20,000 ransom. The dead
bodies were found, however, before
the Mission or officials could con-
tact the outlaws.

Fears that Rev. and Mrs. A. E.
Kohfield, American missionaries
stationed at Tunki, not far from
Tsingteh, had met with a similar
fate or had at least fallen into
Communist hands, were allayed to-
day by direct word from them.

Children Said Safe

A message received by the
Mission headquarters in Shanghai
said that they and their four chil-
dren were so far safe and un-
harmed although a large horde of
Communists are believed to be
heading in the direction of Tunki.

They are prevented from evacuat-
ing because of broken bridges and
condition of the road making motor
car travel impossible. It may be
necessary for the entire group to
start walking. Rev. and Mrs. Koh-
field are natives of Bend, Oregon.

Vice-Consul Sent
(United Press)

NANKING, Dec. 13.—Vice-Consul
Douglas Jenkins, of the American
Legation was sent to Wuhu today
to conduct an investigation into
the circumstances surrounding the
capture of Mr. and Mrs. J. C. Stam
and their infant daughter by
communist bandits.

The Vice-Consul was also in-
structed to make inquiries concern-
ing the whereabouts of the bandits
after departing from Tsingteh on
Sunday.

It is the unofficial opinion of the
members of the American Lega-
tion that the bandits, about two
hundred strong, are now moving
rapidly away from Tsingteh in an
effort to escape capture by the
government's troops.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与美商日报》，1934年12月14日，星期五

安徽匪徒
杀害传教士

两名美国人死于
青弋江城袭击

上海的中国内地会收到一封简略的电报，确认了美国传教士约翰·斯坦姆先生及其妻子（可能）死亡的消息，两人于12月10日在安徽南部青弋江镇的袭击中被匪徒俘虏。电报称他们的尸体已在距离青弋江约七英里的庙桥被发现。

由于缺乏细节，电报仅写道：“省长报告在庙桥发现约翰·贝蒂·斯坦姆的尸体”，因此不确定提到的“贝蒂·斯坦姆”是指斯坦姆夫人，还是指12月10日与父母一同被俘的两个月半大的婴儿女儿。

新近抵达

斯坦姆夫妇是传教领域相对较新的成员，在得到官方保证安全后，最近才返回青弋江驻地。但在他们返回后不久，匪徒突然袭击该镇，将他们掳走。

斯坦姆先生是新泽西州帕特森（Paterson）人。斯坦姆夫人是目前驻济南的美国长老会传教团C. E. 斯科特博士夫妇的女儿。

搜寻凶手
（合众社）

华盛顿，12月13日.—美国副国务卿威廉·菲利普斯三世（William Phillips III）今日表示，相信中国国民政府和安徽省当局将尽一切努力逮捕约翰·斯坦姆牧师夫妇的凶手。

斯坦姆夫妇的尸体在安徽南部距离青弋江约10英里的庙桥被发现，美国传教士即在此地被一群据信是共产党的匪徒俘虏。他们同样被绑架的四个月大的孩子的下落尚未查明。

新人入行

这对夫妇隶属于中国内地会青弋江站，从事传教工作时间不长。斯坦姆牧师是新泽西州帕特森人，斯坦姆夫人虽出生在中国，但曾在芝加哥附近的惠顿学院（Wheaton College）就读。

伊丽莎白·斯科特·斯坦姆（Elizabeth Scott Stam）夫人，在朋友中被称为“贝蒂”，是山东济南美国长老会传教团C. E. 斯科特博士夫妇的女儿。

逃生无门

根据上海中国内地会总部收到的一封由斯坦姆牧师在被共产党俘虏后写的信，由于红军的攻击突然且出乎意料，他们没有时间逃跑。信中说，绑架者索要20,000美元赎金。然而，在传教团或官员能够联系到歹徒之前，就发现了尸体。

对于驻扎在距青弋江不远的屯溪的美国传教士A. E. 科菲尔德（A. E. Kohfield）牧师夫妇遭遇类似命运或至少落入共产党手中的担忧，今日因直接收到他们的消息而得以消除。

称儿童安全

传教团上海总部收到的一条消息说，尽管据信大批共产党人正朝屯溪方向进发，但他们和他们的四个孩子目前安全且未受伤害。

由于桥梁断裂和道路状况导致汽车无法通行，他们无法撤离。整个群体可能不得不开始步行。科菲尔德牧师夫妇是俄勒冈州本德（Bend）人。

派遣副领事
（合众社）

南京，12月13日.—美国公使馆副领事道格拉斯·詹金斯今日被派往芜湖，调查J. C. 斯坦姆先生夫妇及其幼女被共产党匪徒俘虏的相关情况。
副领事还奉命调查匪徒周日离开青弋江后的行踪。
美国公使馆成员的非官方意见认为，这股约两百人的匪徒现在正迅速远离青弋江，试图逃避政府军的抓捕。

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 18, 1934

BABY STAM IS NOW
SAFE IN WUHU

Investigations Into
Double Murder Are
Being Made

NANKING, Dec. 17.—An investigation into the murder of Mr. and Mrs. C. Stam, American missionaries who were killed on December 8 at Miaochiao, 20 miles from their station at Tsingteh, is being carried out at Wuhu by American consular and Chinese officials.

The report that Helen Stam, the three-months-old baby of the murdered missionaries, who escaped death at the hands of the marauders, is at present safe at Wuhu, was confirmed to-day by a message from the Chinese authorities at Wuhu.

Mr. George Atcheson, Jr., the American Consul, is at present at Wuhu collecting information regarding the slaying of the two Americans. Close attention to the case is being paid by Foreign Office officials. Mr. Kuangson Young, Special Commissioner for Foreign Affairs, was instructed to proceed to Wuhu from Hankow to investigate the matter. He is expected to arrive there to-day.

As soon as the Chinese authorities here received word of the capture of the American missionaries, they telegraphed to the local military authorities to endeavour by every possible means to rescue Mr. and Mrs. Stam. The news of the death of the missionaries has been received with the greatest regret by the local authorities who have ordered the Wuhu officials to arrest the murderers and punish them in accordance with the law.
—Reuter.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1934年12月18日，星期二

斯坦姆婴儿现已
在芜湖安然无恙

正在调查
双重谋杀案

南京，12月17日电。——美国领事官员和中国官员正在芜湖对12月8日在距其驻地青德（Tsingteh）20英里的庙桥（Miaochiao）被杀害的美国传教士斯坦姆（C. Stam）夫妇的谋杀案进行调查。

据来自芜湖中国当局的消息证实，此前有报告称，遇害传教士三个月大的婴儿海伦·斯坦姆（Helen Stam）在匪徒手中幸免于难，目前她在芜湖安全无恙。

美国副领事乔治·艾奇逊（George Atcheson, Jr.）先生目前正在芜湖收集有关这两名美国人被杀的信息。外交部官员正密切关注此案。外交特派员杨光燊（Kuangson Young，音译）先生已奉命从汉口前往芜湖调查此事。预计他将于今日抵达那里。

此间中国当局一获悉美国传教士被捕的消息，便致电当地军事当局，要求尽一切可能营救斯坦姆夫妇。地方当局对传教士的死讯表示极为痛惜，并已命令芜湖官员逮捕凶手并依法惩处。
——路透社。

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 15, 1934

Fate Of Stams' Baby Still
Unknown In Shanghai

Deaths Of Parents Near Tsingteh Confirmed By
Telegram, But No Mention Made Of Child;
Hayman And Bossart Remain Captives

No further news has been received late yesterday afternoon by the China Inland Mission here concerning the fate of three-months-old Helen Priscilla Stam, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. John Stam, missionaries who were killed shortly after their capture at Tsingteh, Anhwei, by a band of communists early this month.

Telegrams received by officials of the Sinza Road institution on Thursday confirmed earlier reports that the missionary-couple had been killed, but no mention was made of the baby girl, it was learned yesterday.

Indeed, so meagre was the information reaching here that the action must be deduced from the facts known beforehand. It was said yesterday that the Communist band must have been a strong one, probably around 2,000, and well armed, as Tsingteh was a fortified town.

Battle Probable

After its capture, the Reds probably made captives of Mr. and Mrs. Stam and their child. A telegram to Wuhu from the Governor of Anhwei merely stated that the bodies of Mr. and Mrs. Stam had been found on the battlefield at Miaochiao. This spot is about 15 miles from Tsingteh, and from the use of the word "battlefield," it was assumed here yesterday that a conflict must have taken place between the Communist and government troops at the place. No details are available concerning the time or cause of the death of the missionaries.

The leader of the red band is also unknown, but it is believed that the group was formed in the mountainous section of Anhwei to the east of Tsingteh.

Mr. Stam first came to China two years ago. Previously he had met his future wife while both were attending school in Chicago. Mrs. Stam was then Miss Elizabeth Alden Scott, daughter of Mr. Charles Ernest Scott, of the American Presbyterian Mission, Tsinan, Shantung. They were married at the home of the bride's parents at Tsinan in October, 1933. Both were full members of the China Inland Mission.

BODIES FOUND ON
BATTLEFIELD

Mr. W. J. Hanna On Way
To Miaochiao For
Identification

NANKING, Dec. 14. — The tragic story of the capture and death of the two American missionaries, Mr. and Mrs. C. J. Stam, was brought to light to-day, although the fate of their infant daughter, Helen, is still unknown.

On December 12 about 3,000 communists made a surprise attack on Tsingteh, about 120 miles south of Nanking, where Mr. and Mrs. Stam were stationed, and captured the city.

After looting the town the communists left the next day carrying with them 10 persons among whom were Mr. and Mrs. Stam and their baby. They proceeded with their victims in a south-west direction towards the mountains from where they had come.

Government troops, however, overtook them at Miaochiao, 50 li from Tsingteh, where a severe engagement took place. Later, among the dead on the battlefield Government troops found the two bodies which were believed to be those of Mr. and Mrs. Stam.

Although the body of their three-months-old daughter has not been found, little hope is held out for her safety.

Another foreign missionary in Tsingteh, believed to be a Spanish Catholic priest, happened to be out of town at the time and thus had a lucky escape from capture.

Meanwhile, United States authorities in China acting under instructions from Washington, have renewed their representations to the Nanking and provincial authorities for vigorous measures to be taken to rescue the child if she is still alive.

It is reported from Wuhu that Mr. W. J. Hanna, superintendent of the China Inland Mission there, left to-day for Miaochiao to bring the bodies of Mr. and Mrs. Stam to Wuhu for identification and burial.—Reuter.

Hayman And Bossart

The Mission remains anxious concerning the welfare of Messrs. Arnolis Hayman and R. A. Bosshardt, for two months captives of a large and well-armed Communist band under the leadership of Ho Lung. They were last heard of at Tungshun, Hunan.

It will be remembered that the pair, together with their wives, the two Hayman children, and Miss Grace Emblem, were captured by the Reds on October 9. The two wives and the children were released almost immediately to start ransom negotiations, and Miss Emblem was given her freedom nine days later when unable to stand the swift pace of the band.

Mrs. Hayman is now in Shanghai anxiously awaiting the negotiations being passed by the Swiss and British representatives up-country with the Chinese Government. No ransom notes have been received for some time, it was stated yesterday.

Mr. Hayman came to China in 1918, and is of British nationality being from Auckland, New Zealand. Mr. Bosshardt came to China in 1922 from Manchester, but is of Swiss nationality.

The band which captured them is also described as being large and well-armed. It came originally from southern Hunan under the leadership of Shio Kih, and then went north and joined forces with Ho Lung in southeastern Szechwan. This combined group then started south eastward under the command of Ho Lung and captured the missionaries in Kweichow. The exact location of the band is not known now, but it is thought that they are hiding in the wilds of Honan.

ANHWEI OUTRAGE

The death of Mr. and Mrs. J. C. Stam, American missionaries, at the hands of a band of brigands in Anhwei, and the unknown fate also of their three-months old child, Helen, will have been learned by all foreigners in China with sincere regret and much indignation. It is disconcerting to learn that in the very central province of China, not so very far from Nanking, and much nearer to Wuhu and Hangchow, there are conditions prevailing in which it is possible for bands of brigands, somewhat conveniently styled as Communists, to operate at will. It is reported that it was only quite recently that Mr. and Mrs. Stam moved up to Wuhu in view of the disorder in this district but that, because of reports that conditions had improved, they had returned to their posts. It is not a sufficiently good explanation to say that it is believed that the outrage was perpetrated by one of the bands of Communists who have been disorganized by the recent anti-Red drive. That drive will have achieved little in the way of permanently good results if roving bands have been left to terrorize scattered districts of the country instead of being swept away along with the rest. From time to time news comes to hand from correspondents in the interior telling of bandits and outlaws, and also of soldiers who stay in the walled and well-protected cities. Although much good work has been done in recent years in making the countryside safer, there is still far too much complacency with regard to the existence of gangs of armed desperadoes and it will only be by the creation of a keener general regard for law and order, by the infusion of a greater sense of duty into the minds of local military and police authorities, and by the creation of purely local machinery for the preservation of personal rights, that an improvement will be brought about. It is sad indeed to think that a foreign man and his wife and a baby daughter should have stood exposed to the senseless and brutal deaths meted out to them because a band of murderous rascals were suffered to exist by those who should have cleaned them up.

《字林西报》，1934年12月15日，星期六

上海仍不知
斯坦姆夫妇婴儿的下落

父母在青德附近遇害一事
已由电报证实，但未提及婴儿；
海曼和博夏特仍被扣押

截至昨日下午晚些时候，驻此间的中国内地会尚未收到关于海伦·普里西拉·斯坦姆（Helen Priscilla Stam）命运的任何进一步消息。海伦是约翰·斯坦姆（John Stam）夫妇三个月大的女儿，其父母在本月初于安徽青德被一伙共产党人俘虏后不久即遭杀害。

据悉，新闸路（Sinza Road）机构的官员于周四收到的电报证实了早先关于这对传教士夫妇已被杀害的报道，但昨日得知，电文中并未提及这名女婴。

事实上，传到这里的消息如此匮乏，以至于必须根据事先已知的事实来推断行动情况。昨日有人说，这伙共产党匪帮实力一定很强，人数可能在2,000人左右，且装备精良，因为青德是一座设防城镇。

可能发生战斗

红军在占领青德后，很可能将斯坦姆夫妇及其孩子作为俘虏带走。安徽省主席发给芜湖的一份电报仅称，斯坦姆夫妇的尸体在庙桥的战场上被发现。该地点距离青德约15英里，根据“战场”一词的使用，这里昨日推测在该地共产党军队与政府军之间一定发生过冲突。关于传教士死亡的时间或原因，暂无细节可供参考。

红军匪帮的头目也不为人知，但据信该团伙是在青德以东的安徽山区组建的。

斯坦姆先生两年前首次来到中国。此前，他在芝加哥求学期间结识了他未来的妻子。斯坦姆夫人当时是伊丽莎白·阿尔登·斯科特小姐（Miss Elizabeth Alden Scott），她是山东济南美国长老会传教士查尔斯·欧内斯特·斯科特（Charles Ernest Scott）先生的女儿。他们于1933年10月在新娘父母位于济南的家中结婚。两人均为中国内地会的正式成员。

尸体发现于
战场

W. J. 汉纳先生正前往
庙桥进行辨认

南京，12月14日电。——两名美国传教士C. J. 斯坦姆夫妇被俘及死亡的悲剧故事今日真相大白，尽管他们幼女海伦的命运仍然未知。

12月12日，约3,000名共产党人对位于南京以南约120英里的青德发动突袭，斯坦姆夫妇即驻守于此，该城随后被攻占。

共产党人在洗劫城镇后于次日离开，带走了10人，其中包括斯坦姆夫妇及其婴儿。他们带着受害者向西南方向的山地进发，那是他们来的地方。

然而，政府军在距青德50里的庙桥追上了他们，并在那里发生了激烈的交战。后来，政府军在战场上的死者中发现了两具尸体，被认为是斯坦姆夫妇。

虽然尚未找到他们三个月大女儿的尸体，但她生还的希望渺茫。

青德的另一名外国传教士，据信是一名西班牙天主教神父，当时碰巧不在城内，因此幸运地逃脱了被俘的命运。

与此同时，在华美国当局根据华盛顿的指示，再次向南京及省级当局提出交涉，要求采取有力措施，如果孩子还活着，务必将其救出。

据芜湖报道，当地中国内地会监督W. J. 汉纳（W. J. Hanna）先生今日启程前往庙桥，将斯坦姆夫妇的遗体运回芜湖进行辨认和安葬。——路透社。

海曼和博夏特

教会方面仍对阿诺利斯·海曼（Arnolis Hayman）和R. A. 博夏特（R. A. Bosshardt）两位先生的安危感到焦虑，他们已被贺龙领导的一支庞大且装备精良的共产党匪帮扣押两个月。最后一次听到他们的消息是在湖南东顺（Tungshun，音译）。

记得这两人连同他们的妻子、两名海曼家的孩子以及格蕾丝·恩布勒姆小姐（Miss Grace Emblem）于10月9日被红军俘虏。两名妻子和孩子几乎立即被释放以启动赎金谈判，而恩布勒姆小姐因无法承受匪帮的快速行军节奏，在九天后获释。

海曼夫人现在上海，焦急地等待瑞士和英国代表在内地与中国政府进行的谈判结果。据悉，已有相当一段时间未收到任何赎金信件。

海曼先生于1918年来华，具有英国国籍，来自新西兰奥克兰。博夏特先生于1922年从曼彻斯特来华，但具有瑞士国籍。

俘虏他们的匪帮也被描述为规模庞大且装备精良。该匪帮最初在史纪（Shio Kih，音译）的领导下来自湖南南部，然后北上，在四川东南部与贺龙部汇合。这支联合部队随后在贺龙的指挥下向东南进发，并在贵州俘虏了传教士。目前尚不清楚该匪帮的确切位置，但据信他们正隐藏在河南的荒野中。

安徽暴行

美国传教士J. C. 斯坦姆夫妇在安徽死于匪帮之手，他们三个月大的孩子海伦的命运也未卜，在华所有外国人获悉此事后无不深感悲痛和愤慨。令人不安的是，在中国的中部省份，离南京并不太远，离芜湖和杭州更近的地方，竟然存在这样的状况，使得被称为“共产党”的匪帮能够方便地随意活动。据报道，斯坦姆夫妇鉴于该地区局势混乱，最近刚搬往芜湖，但因听说局势好转，又回到了岗位。如果说这起暴行被认为是由近期反共围剿中被击溃的共产党匪帮之一所为，这并不能构成充分的解释。如果流窜匪帮未被彻底清除，而是任其恐吓国家的零星地区，那么这次围剿在取得持久良好成果方面将收效甚微。不时有来自内地的通讯员消息传来，讲述土匪和不法之徒的情况，以及那些待在城墙坚固、防护良好的城市里的士兵。尽管近年来在使乡村更加安全方面做了大量有益的工作，但对于武装亡命之徒团伙的存在仍然过于自满，只有通过增强全社会对法律和秩序的重视，向地方军事和警察当局灌输更强的责任感，并建立纯粹的地方机制以保护个人权利，才能带来改善。想到一个外国男子、他的妻子和一个女婴，因为那些本应清除他们的人容忍了一群杀人恶棍的存在，而不得不面对毫无意义且残酷的死亡，这确实令人悲哀。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 14, 1934

U. S. MISSIONARIES'
BODIES FOUND

Mr. And Mrs. Stam Met
Death At Hands Of
Communists

SMALL HOPE HELD FOR
SAFETY OF CHILD

A telegram received here by the
China Inland Mission last night,
stating that the murdered bodies
of Mr. and Mrs. J. C. Stam had
been found 40 li from Tsingteh,
where they were captured by
bandits several days ago, definite-
ly sealed the fate of the two U. S.
missionaries. Whether their three-
month-old daughter Helen also.
met her death at the hands of the
brigands had not been confirmed
up to a late hour last night, but
the chances for her safety are said
to be remote.

Mr. Stam is a native of New
Jersey and had only been in China
two years, while his wife is the
daughter of Dr. and Mrs. C. E.
Scott, of the American Presby-
terias Mission in Tsinan, Shantung
Province.

One of the tragic features of the
whole story lies in the fact that
owing to disorder in their district
and the ill-health of Mrs. Stam,
the family recently went to Wuhu,
but Mr. Stam returned to their
mission and, upon being officially
assured that there was no longer
any danger, hastened to bring
back his wife and small daughter.
They had been back only a short
while when they were captured.

Although no actual confirmation
has been received, it is generally
believed that the outrage was per-
petrated by one of the bands of
communists who have been dis-
organized by the recent anti-Red
drive and who are at present rov-
ing about in quite large bands,
terrorizing the inhabitants of the
district.

The moment it was definitely
known that the missionaries had
been captured, the matter was put
in the hands of the U. S. authori-
ties, and on Tuesday, Mr. Willis
R. Peck, Counsellor of the Ameri-
can Legation (resident in Nan-
king) called on the Foreign Office
and the officials of the Anhwei
Provincial Government to request
them to take all possible steps to
secure the release of the prisoners.
Meanwhile, Mr. W. J. Hanna,
Superintendent for Anhwei of the
China Island Missions, left the
council meeting in Shanghai and
ran a losing race with death to get
in touch with the brigands, and
save the captives.

PARIS, Dec. 18. — Late last
night, the French Chamber of
Deputies adopted, by 312 votes to
267, the Government Bill for re-
organization of the wheat market.
—Havas.

美国传教士
尸体被发现

斯坦姆夫妇
死于共产党人之手

儿童安全
希望渺茫

中国内地会昨晚在此收到一份电报，称J. C. 斯坦姆夫妇的被杀尸体已在距青德40里处被发现，几天前他们正是在那里被匪徒俘虏的，这最终确定了两名美国传教士的命运。截至昨晚深夜，尚未确认他们三个月大的女儿海伦是否也死于匪徒之手，但据说她生还的机会渺茫。

斯坦姆先生是新泽西州人，来华仅两年，而他的妻子是山东济南美国长老会传教士C. E. 斯科特博士夫妇的女儿。

整个事件的悲剧性特征之一在于，由于所在地区的混乱以及斯坦姆夫人的健康状况不佳，这家人最近去了芜湖，但斯坦姆先生返回了他们的传教站，并在得到官方保证不再有任何危险后，急忙接回妻子和小女儿。他们回来不久便被俘虏。

虽然尚未收到实际确认，但人们普遍认为，这起暴行是由近期反共围剿中被击溃、目前正以大股形式流窜并恐吓该地区居民的共产党匪帮之一所为。

一旦确切得知传教士被俘，此事便交由美国当局处理。周二，美国公使馆参赞（驻南京）威利斯·R. 佩克（Willis R. Peck）先生拜访了外交部及安徽省政府官员，请求他们采取一切可能步骤确保囚犯获释。与此同时，中国内地会安徽区监督W. J. 汉纳先生离开上海的理事会会议，与死神赛跑，试图联系匪徒并营救人质。

巴黎，12月18日电。——昨晚深夜，法国众议院以312票对267票通过了政府提出的小麦市场重组法案。——哈瓦斯社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY. DECEMBER 13, 1931

U. S. MISSIONARIES
ARE CAPTURED

Legation Asks That
Investigation Be
Started

NANKING, Dec. 12.—Mr.
Willis R. Peck, Counsellor of the
American Legation (resident in
Nanking), called on the Foreign
Office this morning regarding the
reported capture by bandits of
Mr. and Mrs. C. J. Stam and their
infant daughter several days ago
at Tsingteh, in South Anhwei,
about 120 miles south of Nanking.
Mr. Peck requested that the
Foreign Office and the Anhwei
Provincial Government ascertain
the veracity of the report, and, if
it were true, take all possible
steps to secure the release of the
captives.
Mr. and Mrs. Stam are mem-
bers of the China Island Mission
who left for Tsingteh from Wuhu
but a short time ago after having
been assured that the district was
safe from bandits.—Reuter.

Report Confirmed
PEIPING, Dec. 12.—Confirma-
tion was received here to-day of
the capture by bandits of Mr. and
Mrs. C. J. Stam and their infant
daughter, Helen, at Tsingteh,
South Anhwei.—Reuter.

美国传教士

公使馆要求
展开调查

南京，12月12日电。——美国驻南京公使馆参赞（常驻南京）威利斯·R·佩克（Willis R. Peck）先生今晨拜访外交部，就数日前在安徽南部青提（Tsingteh，音译，距南京以南约120英里）发生的C. J. 斯塔姆（Stam）夫妇及其幼女据报被匪徒绑架一事进行交涉。佩克先生请求外交部及安徽省政府核实该报道的真实性，若属实，则采取一切可能措施以确保人质获释。斯塔姆夫妇系“中国内地会”（China Island Mission，原文如此，通常指China Inland Mission）成员，此前在得到该地区无匪患的保证后，不久刚从芜湖前往青提。——路透社。

消息获证实
北平，12月12日电。——今日在此收到确认消息，C. J. 斯塔姆夫妇及其幼女海伦（Helen）在安徽南部青提被匪徒绑架。——路透社。

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE MURDER OF STAM AND HIS WIFE

The report of the death of Stam, an American
missionary, and his wife at the hands of Communists at
Tsingteh Hsien, Anhwei, has already been published by
Chinese and foreign newspapers at Nanking and Shanghai.
As the story given by these newspapers might not be
complete or accurate, the following information has been
secured from various reliable sources.
Tsingteh Hsien, lying in the southern part
of Anhwei, is on the border of Kiangsi and Chekiang. It
is surrounded by mountains and is very inaccessible. No
telephonic or telegraphic facilities are provided.
A number of straggling Communists from
Kiangsi first invaded Chang Hwa (昌化), Chekiang, but
after suffering a defeat at the hands of government troops,
the marauders headed for the south of Anhwei. On the
way thither, they were again intercepted by government
troops. The Communists then invaded Tsingteh Hsien. As
no militia had been organized by the city, it fell into
the hands of the roving Communists on December 6 last year.
On the following day, the city was re-captured by the
government troops.
Informed that an American missionary had
been captured by the Communists, the government troops
gave chase and a fierce engagement lasting four hours
took place at Miao Shu (庙首). The Communists were
again defeated but unfortunately the American missionary
Stam and his wife had already been killed.

将需要兵力在中国海域提供保护。
同时，莫斯利先生请求约翰·西蒙爵士建议中国政府，由英国海军力量与中国政府联合派遣舰艇剿灭海盗。虽然中国视此为难以忍受的问题，但某国却对此深感满意，并认为这是一个绝佳的机会。
假设英国下议院就此问题通过决议成为事实，该国将以保护其商船为借口，派遣军舰在中国海域巡航。一旦与其勾结的海盗袭击某艘船只，其部队将以追剿海盗为由在任何地点登陆。若出现这种情况，纠纷自然会发生。
中国海军因财政困难而受限，无法为我们的渔民提供充分的保护，允许其他国家的渔民在我国海域活动，致使海盗行为猖獗。既然设有海军部，其职责应是肃清海盗之害，并防止其他国家以此为借口进行干涉。

《时报》及其他本地报刊：

斯塔姆及其妻子遇害案

关于美国传教士斯塔姆及其妻子在安徽青提县被共产党人杀害的报道，已见于南京和上海的中文及外文报刊。鉴于这些报刊提供的消息可能不完整或不准确，现从各种可靠来源获取如下信息。
青提县位于安徽南部，地处江西和浙江边界。该县群山环绕，交通极为不便。未设电话或电报设施。
一批来自江西的零散共产党人首先侵入浙江昌化，但在被政府军击败后，匪众向安徽南部进发。在途中，他们再次遭到政府军的拦截。随后，共产党人侵入青提县。由于该城未组织民团，于去年12月6日落入流窜的共产党人手中。次日，政府军收复该城。
政府军获悉一名美国传教士被共产党人俘虏后，随即展开追击，在庙首（Miao Shu）发生了一场持续四小时的激烈战斗。共产党人再次战败，但不幸的是，美国传教士斯塔姆及其妻子已被杀害。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY. DECEMBER 15, 1934 


ANHWEI OUTRAGE 

The death of Mr. and Mrs, J. C. Stam, 
American missionaries, at the hands of a 
band of brigands in Anhwci, and the 
unknown fate also of their three-months old 
child, Helen, will have been learned by all 
foreigners in China with sincere regret and 
much indignation. It is disconcerting to learn 
that in the very central province of China, 
not so very far from Nanking, and much 
ne rer to Wuhu and Hangchow, there are 
conditions prevailing in which it is possible 
tor bands of brigands, somewhat conveniently 
styled as Communists, to operate at will. It 
is reported that it was only quite recently 
that Mr. and Mrs. Stam moved up to Wuhu 
in view of the disorder in this district but 
that, because of reports that conditions had 
improved, they had returned to their posts. 
It is not a sufficiently good explanation to 
say that it is believed that the outrage was 
perpetrated by one of the bands of Com- 
munists who have been disorganized by the 
recent anti-Red drive. That drive will have 
achieved little in the way of permanently 
good results if roving bands have been left 
to terrorize scattered districts of the country 
instead of being swept away along with the 
rest. From time to time news comes to hand 
from correspondents in the interior telling of 
bandits and outlaws, and also of soldiers who 


‘stay in the walled and well-protected cities. 


Although much good work has been done in 
recent years in making the countryside safer, 
there is still far too much complacency with 
regard to the existence of gangs of armed 
desperadoes and it will only be by the crea- 
tion of a keener general regard for law and 
order, by the infusion of a greater sense of 


‘duty into the minds of loca) military and 
police authorities, and by the creation of. 


purely local machinery for the preservation 


Be personal rights, that an improvement will 


e brought about. It is sad indeed to think 


that a foreign man and his wife and a baby 
daughter should have stood exposed to the 
senseless and brutal deaths 
them because a band of murderous rascals 
were suffered to exist by those who should 
have cleaned them up.
